findings.detail: The ticket description requires a non-author reviewer to post the 73-row TSV PASS receipt. The ticket was authored by 'Rebar Bot' (author_id: 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d, author_email: joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com). Both TSV receipt comments (comments[1] and comments[2]) and the independent review comment (comments[3]) were all posted by 'RebarBotNava' with the same author_id 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d and author_email joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com — the same identity that authored the ticket. The reviewer_session in all 73 rows is '/root/implement_core_test_comments/review_de77_final_clean'. The ticket specification states 'Missing, duplicate, extra, author-reviewed, or non-PASS rows block closure.' Since the receipt was posted by the same bot identity that authored the ticket, the 'non-author reviewer' requirement is not satisfied by what is visible in the ticket snapshot I read.
findings.remediation: A human reviewer (not the Rebar Bot identity 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d) must post the 73-row TSV PASS receipt as a ticket comment, citing the merged commit SHA (8b9aa194fbc96017bbda9d7b8df1f4eb418fb98d or the reviewed tree dfd6f8e6b3051cbdceec6cbe4d2f19887b200bc6), with their own reviewer_session and author identity distinct from the ticket author.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
